basics.name: Dharini Raghavan
basics.label: Ph.D. Student, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology
basics.summary: I develop representation-learning methods for biomedical imaging, generative modeling, and embodied perception. My research asks how images, signals, language, and geometry can be mapped into latent variables that are predictive, calibrated, mechanistically interpretable, and stable under distribution shift. The common thread across my work is state modeling: learning compact representations of biological or physical systems from partial, noisy observations.

researchProfile.headline: Representation learning, generative modeling, biomedical AI, and embodied perception
researchProfile.summary: My research develops AI systems that infer biological or physical state from partial, noisy, high-dimensional observations. I work across medical foundation models, oculomics, computational pathology, vision-language quality representation learning, flow-based generative geometry, vascular and cardiac world models, clinical survival modeling, uncertainty and calibration, and 3D perception for robotics.
coreThemes: Representation learning from biomedical images, signals, language, and geometry
Generative modeling, flow-based probability transport, and topology-preserving synthesis
Patient-state and disease-state modeling from partial observations
Medical foundation models for retinal imaging, OCT/OCTA, pathology, CT, and cine MRI
Vision-language models for zero-shot quality representation learning
Uncertainty, calibration, external validation, and robustness under distribution shift
Embodied perception, zero-shot localization, SLAM, differentiable 3D scene representation, and edge AI

education.summary: Advisor: Prof. Anant Madabhushi. Focus on representation learning, medical foundation models, generative modeling, clinical AI, and computer vision.
Coursework: machine learning, MRI physics, biomedical sensing, advanced programming, MEMS.

researchPrograms.name: Foundation AI for reasoning, reliability, and generative state modeling
researchPrograms.summary: Developing methods that study how modern AI systems reason, represent uncertainty, and model evolving biological state.
highlights: LLM diagnostic reasoning as constrained inference under mutually exclusive disease hypotheses, causal exclusion, noisy observations, and calibration stress tests.
Flow-based generative geometry through the analysis of velocity fields, interpolants, probability-transport paths, distributional asymmetries, curvature, and likelihood calibration.
Physics-consistent vascular world models that simulate plausible organ-specific vascular states conditioned on tissue context, disease progression, and intervention.

researchPrograms.name: Zero-shot quality representation learning for robust vision
researchPrograms.summary: Developing EyeQC, a zero-shot method for learning image-quality representations from frozen vision-language embeddings.
highlights: Models acquisition quality as latent directions induced by semantic prompt contrasts.
Enables continuous multi-axis scoring of focus, illumination, contrast, field of view, occlusion, and artifacts without supervised quality labels.
Supports failure-mode decomposition, retrieval, batch-shift analysis, and quality-aware downstream learning.
Extended to curriculum-based visual acuity prediction from fundus images, using image quality as both a reliability signal and an ordering prior for robust regression.

researchPrograms.name: Oculomics for systemic risk modeling
researchPrograms.summary: Developing statistical-learning and representation-learning frameworks that use ocular structure as a non-invasive projection of systemic disease state.
highlights: OCTA capillary remodeling biomarkers for coronary microvascular dysfunction in women with INOCA.
CORI: retinal cardiovascular risk index for cardiovascular risk prediction in cancer patients.
Retinal vascular and perivascular geometry for cardio-renal-metabolic risk.
Deep fundus representations for pan-cancer risk modeling and cardiovascular risk in cancer patients.
3D OCT-derived morphology for disease phenotyping and treatment-response modeling.

researchPrograms.name: Topology-preserving generative modeling for cross-modal imaging
researchPrograms.summary: Developed frequency-disentangled generative modeling for unpaired fundus-to-OCTA synthesis.
highlights: Factorizes image translation into low-frequency appearance transport and high-frequency anatomical topology preservation.
Constrains the generative map to preserve vessel geometry, connectivity, and microvascular structure while adapting modality-specific image statistics.
Reframes medical image generation as structure-preserving distribution alignment under weak supervision.

researchPrograms.name: Spatial risk-field learning in computational pathology
researchPrograms.summary: Developing MarginCall, a multitask whole-slide learning framework for breast surgical margin assessment.
highlights: Treats residual disease risk as structured prediction over tissue geometry rather than a single endpoint label.
Learns coupled tumor-probability fields, margin-distance representations, morphology embeddings, and uncertainty maps.
Uses intermediate network states as interpretable measurements for failure analysis, power analysis, and spatial phenotype discovery.

researchPrograms.name: Spatial pathology biomarkers in multiple myeloma
researchPrograms.summary: Investigating plasma-cell and immune-cell organization as a structured tissue system in bone marrow biopsies.
highlights: Uses deep learning and spatial tissue modeling to quantify neighborhood geometry, local composition, immune-plasma interaction patterns, and architecture-level phenotypes.
Studies sex-specific survival differences in multiple myeloma using spatial pathology biomarkers.

researchPrograms.name: Generative state-space modeling of 4D cardiac dynamics
researchPrograms.summary: Exploring foundation-model methods for cine cardiac MRI that learn compact latent trajectories of cardiac motion, morphology, and remodeling from spatiotemporal image sequences.
highlights: Frames cardiac video as a generative state-space problem.
Combines representation learning, temporal attention, neural dynamics, geometry-aware embeddings, and counterfactual trajectory modeling to infer hidden physiological state.

researchPrograms.name: Generalist CT foundation models
researchPrograms.summary: Developed target-adaptive CT diagnosis systems for the CVPR 2026 Foundation Models for General CT Image Diagnosis Challenge.
highlights: Frames general CT diagnosis as representation selection under heterogeneous evidence regimes.
Studies aggregation operators, calibration strategies, and inductive biases for localized organ findings, diffuse systemic patterns, and chest disease.
Ranked 3rd in the validation phase.

work.name: Madabhushi Lab, Georgia Tech & Emory University School of Medicine
work.summary: Advisor: Prof. Anant Madabhushi. Conducting research at the intersection of medical foundation models, oculomics, computational pathology, generative modeling, clinical survival learning, and multimodal patient-state modeling.
highlights: Leading and contributing to projects on retinal biomarkers of systemic disease, pathology spatial risk fields, vision-language quality geometry, vascular and cardiac world models, and generalist medical imaging foundation models.

LLM reasoning in medicine: benchmarking whether large language models perform diagnostic reasoning as structured inference or collapse toward prevalence priors under constrained clinical cases. [ICLR'26 Workshop; Stanford AIMI Symposium]
Flow-based generative geometry: analyzing velocity fields, interpolants, transport paths, curvature, density concentration, likelihood calibration, and representation asymmetries.
Physics-consistent vascular world models: generative agents for plausible vascular state modeling under tissue context, disease, and intervention.

EyeQC: zero-shot quality representation learning from frozen VLM embeddings for multi-axis quality scoring, failure-mode decomposition, retrieval, batch-shift analysis, and quality-aware downstream learning. [ARVO'26 Hot Topic]
Oculomics for systemic risk modeling: retinal imaging biomarkers for CMD, cardio-oncology risk, cardio-renal-metabolic risk, pan-cancer risk, and 3D OCT morphology. [AJPC'26; ACC'26]
Frequency-disentangled generative modeling: topology-preserving unpaired fundus-to-OCTA synthesis.

Spatial risk-field learning: multitask deep learning for breast surgical margin assessment through tumor-probability fields, margin-distance maps, morphology embeddings, and uncertainty maps. [ARPA-H collaboration]

work.name: ViTAL Lab, Georgia Tech & Emory University School of Medicine
work.summary: Advisor: Prof. Hyeokhyen Kwon. Wearable AI for cognitive health and robustness in clinical sensing.
highlights: Developed multimodal sensing and interpretable machine-learning models for mild cognitive impairment using wearable IMU and ambient sensing.
Formulated gait, balance, and behavior as noisy longitudinal observations of cognitive and functional state.
Emphasized clinically interpretable digital biomarkers and subgroup robustness. [AMIA'25 Podium Presentation; PLOS Digital Health under review]
Analyzed how demographic heterogeneity, feature distributions, and clinical covariates shape prediction error in longitudinal sensing models.

work.name: AI & Robotics Technology Park (ARTPARK), Indian Institute of Science
work.summary: Advisor: Prof. Bharadwaj Amrutur. Research on foundation-model perception, embodied localization, and differentiable 3D scene representation.
highlights: Developed zero-shot embodied localization methods combining foundation-model visual embeddings, keypoint geometry, and spatial consistency constraints.
Improved RTAB-Map SLAM accuracy by more than 63% without task-specific fine-tuning. [ACM ICVGIP'24]
Advanced multi-camera pose refinement using anisotropic Gaussian primitives, SE(3) optimization, and differentiable rendering for infrastructure-assisted robot localization.

work.name: Autonomous Machines Lab, Indian Institute of Science
work.summary: Advisor: Prof. Bharadwaj Amrutur. Research on uncertainty-aware multi-robot perception, edge AI, and neural compression.
highlights: Designed fixed-camera localization systems for multiple robots under occlusion, clutter, and sensor noise.
Used ensemble disagreement, Monte Carlo dropout, and spatial uncertainty maps to quantify pose reliability.
Applied structured pruning, INT8 quantization, and cross-architecture distillation for real-time 6-DoF pose estimation on Qualcomm RB5 platforms.
Achieved more than 3x speedup with less than 2% accuracy degradation. [Qualcomm Developer Symposium]

work.name: NOKIA Networked Robotics Centre, Indian Institute of Science
work.summary: Advisors: Prof. Bharadwaj Amrutur and Dr. Raghu Krishnapuram. Research on infrastructure-camera localization and sim-to-real perception for GPS-denied robot navigation.
highlights: Developed high-precision visual localization for GPS-denied robot navigation using keypoint correspondences, geometric consistency, and 6-DoF pose estimation.
Enabled sub-centimeter positioning for safe human-robot collaboration.
Built synthetic-data generation pipelines with domain randomization over lighting, texture, pose, and occlusion.
Generated 100K+ annotated images and achieved less than 5% degradation on real-world deployment.

work.name: FIST Lab, Indian Institute of Science
work.position: Summer Research Fellow, Indian Academy of Sciences
work.summary: Advisor: Dr. Jayaprakash. Research on medical image restoration and 3D tumor localization.
highlights: Designed lightweight residual CNNs for non-blind 3D deconvolution of clinical MRI scans.
Improved PSNR by more than 2.5 dB over Richardson-Lucy baselines with more than 10x faster inference.
Extended the restoration framework to photoacoustic tomography for 3D tumor localization.

work.name: Indian Institute of Technology Indore
work.summary: Advisor: Dr. Neelima Satyam. Research on geospatial machine learning for hazard prediction.
highlights: Built ensemble-learning pipelines combining geospatial covariates, geological databases, and GeoTIFF imagery for landslide susceptibility mapping and spatial risk visualization.

projects.name: LLM Reasoning in Medicine
projects.description: Investigating whether large language models perform diagnostic reasoning as structured inference or collapse toward prevalence priors under constrained clinical cases. Frames medical LLM evaluation around constraint satisfaction, causal exclusion, evidence integration, and calibration under noisy observations.

projects.name: Flow-based Generative Geometry
projects.description: Studying generative modeling through the geometry of probability transport. Analyzes learned velocity fields, interpolants, transport paths, curvature, density concentration, likelihood calibration, and representation asymmetries along the generative path.

projects.name: Physics-Consistent Vascular World Models
projects.description: Developing vascular world models where generative agents learn plausible, physics-consistent vascular states conditioned on tissue context, disease state, and intervention. Treats vascular morphology as a structured generative object where branching topology, perfusion constraints, remodeling, angiogenesis, and treatment response are modeled as coupled state transitions rather than static image features.

projects.name: Zero-shot Quality Representation Learning for Robust Vision
projects.description: Developing EyeQC, a zero-shot method for learning image-quality representations from frozen vision-language embeddings. The framework models acquisition artifacts as latent quality directions induced by semantic prompt contrasts, enabling continuous, multi-axis scoring without supervised quality labels.

projects.name: Oculomics for Systemic Risk Modeling
projects.description: Developing statistical-learning and representation-learning frameworks that use ocular structure as a non-invasive projection of systemic disease state. Includes OCTA capillary remodeling for CMD, CORI for cardiovascular risk in cancer patients, perivascular geometry for cardio-renal-metabolic risk, deep fundus representations for pan-cancer risk modeling, and 3D OCT morphology for treatment-response modeling.

projects.name: Frequency-Disentangled Generative Modeling for Topology-Preserving Synthesis
projects.description: Developed an unpaired cross-modal generation framework that factorizes image translation into low-frequency appearance transport and high-frequency anatomical topology preservation. Applied to fundus-to-OCTA synthesis.

projects.name: Spatial Risk-Field Learning for Surgical Margin Assessment
projects.description: Developing a multitask deep learning framework that treats surgical margin assessment in breast cancer resections as structured prediction over tissue geometry. The model learns coupled tumor-probability fields, margin-distance representations, morphology embeddings, and uncertainty maps.

projects.name: Generative State-Space Modeling of 4D Cardiac Dynamics
projects.description: Exploring foundation-model methods for cine cardiac MRI that learn compact latent trajectories of cardiac motion, morphology, and remodeling from spatiotemporal image sequences.

projects.name: Spatial Pathology Biomarkers in Multiple Myeloma
projects.description: Investigating plasma-cell and immune-cell organization from bone marrow biopsies using deep learning and spatial tissue modeling. Extracts neighborhood geometry, local composition, immune-plasma interaction patterns, and architecture-level phenotypes associated with sex-specific survival differences.

projects.name: Generalist CT Foundation Models
projects.description: Developed target-adaptive CT diagnosis systems for the CVPR Foundation Models for General CT Image Diagnosis Challenge. Frames general CT diagnosis as representation selection under heterogeneous evidence regimes.

projects.name: 3D OCT Biomarker Detection
projects.description: Developed multi-branch deep learning models for volumetric OCT biomarker classification, combining spatial and spectral feature streams, late fusion, and gradient-based interpretability; achieved >98.5% macro F1-score.

projects.name: Wearable Bioimpedance Sensing for Tendon Health Monitoring
projects.description: Engineered real-time bioimpedance and IMU sensing for tendon strain and tissue-state discrimination. Modeled impedance variation as a physiologically constrained signal linked to tendon deformation and injury state.

projects.name: Hybrid Bi-LSTM--Transformer for Preterm Birth Prediction
projects.description: Developed recurrent-attention models for spontaneous preterm-labor prediction from multi-channel electrohysterogram signals, combining temporal gating, self-attention, and neural compression; achieved >96% accuracy and >3x inference speedup.

projects.name: Multimodal Neuroimaging for Alzheimer's Disease
projects.description: Developed machine-learning pipelines for Alzheimer's disease classification using multimodal MRI-PET fusion and neuroimaging feature representations.
tags: Journal of Machine Learning for Modeling and Computing'23

projects.name: Sparse Ensemble Networks for UAV Detection and Tracking
projects.description: Designed sparse ensembles for miniaturized UAV detection, drone-bird discrimination, and RGB/IR localization under low illumination, clutter, and distortion; achieved >5x inference speedup and >25% relative localization improvement.

projects.name: NIR Spectroscopy-Based Non-Invasive Glucometer
projects.description: Designed a near-infrared sensing and neural calibration system for non-invasive glucose estimation using particle-swarm optimization and Clarke Error Grid validation.

projects.name: Vision-Guided Robotic Manipulation for Sericulture
projects.description: Implemented instance segmentation and 6-DoF inverse-kinematics control for autonomous sorting of diseased versus healthy silkworms, integrating mask prediction, grasp localization, and class-conditioned manipulation.

projects.name: Lightweight Cardiac Sound Classification and Wearable Monitoring
projects.description: Developed lightweight deep ensemble models with attention mechanisms for cardiac sound classification, later extending the system toward edge-to-cloud vital-sign monitoring, PPG-derived HRV extraction, oscillometric blood-pressure estimation, and telemedicine integration.

projects.name: Wearable Textile Antenna Performance Prediction
projects.description: Developed ant-colony-optimized support vector regression models for performance prediction of wearable textile antennas.

projects.name: 3D Medical Image Deconvolution
projects.description: Designed lightweight residual CNNs for non-blind 3D deconvolution of clinical MRI scans, improving PSNR by more than 2.5 dB over Richardson-Lucy baselines with more than 10x faster inference. Extended the restoration framework to photoacoustic tomography for 3D tumor localization.

projects.name: Geospatial ML for Hazard Prediction
projects.description: Built ensemble-learning pipelines combining geospatial covariates, geological databases, and GeoTIFF imagery for landslide susceptibility mapping and spatial risk visualization.
